bug_semantics: Authenticated account follow and notification-mutation endpoints were registered as GET (/account/follow, /account/delete_notification, /account/mark_notification_read, /account/mark_all_read). A third-party page can induce the victim browser to send those cookie-authenticated GETs, so CSRF can follow/unfollow a user or delete/mark notifications. The patch switches the routes to POST/DELETE and sends X-CSRFToken from the templates.
flaw_origin: 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 (ecrou-exact, add: [social] notifications, follows, reports, system logs and admin panels) first added the four GET handlers in website/web/account/account.py. Parent 45874f5d162c4dc640f1763cb9916bccaf62b261 already had that file but none of those routes. Later e502ee7c1cfd and 672ca701b393 only extended or renamed surrounding account code; methods=['GET'] on those four routes is unchanged until the fix.
evidence: CVE-2026-73162 is PUBLISHED (CIRCL; GHSA withdrawn_at null). git log -S "route(\"/follow\", methods=['GET'])" (and the three sibling GET route strings) on website/web/account/account.py hits only 4fa058f3 (write) and c352c232 (GET->POST/DELETE). Parent-tree check: git cat-file -e 45874f5d:website/web/account/account.py succeeds; grep of those four route("/...") strings on the parent file exits 1. BIC is a single-parent commit, not a squash. git cat-file -p 4fa058f3 shows author/committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> and trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>. git log -1 --format='%an %ae %cn %ce' 4fa058f3: ecrou-exact geffetheo@gmail.com ecrou-exact geffetheo@gmail.com. Advisory fix c352c232 (Christian Studer, human, no AI trailer) changes the four methods=['GET'] to POST/DELETE on account.py and adds X-CSRFToken in the calling templates. ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29: numactl git show 4fa058f^:website/web/account/account.py | grep -c 'route("/follow"' = 0 while BIC 4fa058f adds "@account_blueprint.route('/follow', methods=['GET'])" at line 237 (plus delete_notification/mark_notification_read/mark_all_read) — state-mutating GET routes new at BIC. -> introducer_parent_absent=true.
reasoning: The vulnerability is CSRF from state-changing GET handlers. Those four GET routes first appear in 4fa058f3, which also carries a canonical Claude Sonnet 4.6 co-author trailer; the parent already had account.py without the routes. AI wrote the defective surface, so the verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The later human fix only remediates method verbs and CSRF headers and does not change BIC authorship.
